column1: Table S3b. Frame-stage SC priority operating regions
Priority operating regions (weight = 2) and IFC implementation evidence; all distances are scenario-modeling parameters.

column2: Inspect completed columns for observable surface defects and geometric discrepancies.
column4: On floors 1–3, free-space bands 0.5–1.5 m from all applicable column faces; retain feasible observation locations and local turning space. Remove structural solids and inaccessible sectors.
column5: Direct IFC: IfcColumn solids, IfcSlab floor support; surface offset + access/visibility test. Evidence: Direct + rule-derived

column2: Inspect accessible concrete beams and beam–column joints using visual/NDT tasks.
column4: On the corresponding supporting floor or safe platform, a 1.5 m offset around the beam horizontal projection and beam–column joint inspection positions; do not designate airborne or solid beam volume as floor-robot space.
column5: Direct IFC: IfcBeam, IfcColumn, IfcSlab; project beam geometry to accessible support plane; verify sensor reach or an inspection platform. Evidence: Direct + rule-derived

column2: Document geometric/surface conditions at completed slab perimeters and true slab openings.
column4: Continuous inward inspection strips 0.5–2.0 m from the true exposed slab perimeter and applicable slab-hole boundaries on floors 1–3; apply safe standoff and exclude voids.
column5: Direct IFC: IfcSlab boundaries and IfcOpeningElement only where related to IfcSlab by IfcRelVoidsElement; inward buffer intersect traversable floor. Evidence: Direct + rule-derived

column2: Mark planned structural reference/grid points on completed supporting floor surfaces.
column4: 1.0 m-radius workstations at selected IfcGrid-axis intersections and projected reference points; connect points first along X-direction grid lines and then Y-direction grid lines with total 1.5 m wide paths.
column5: Direct IFC: IfcGrid axes (if provided), IfcColumn locations, IfcSlab surfaces; ground projection and access clipping. Marks are planned, not surveyed control observations. Evidence: IFC + layout task rule

column2: Move small structural tools/materials from access to designated active work bays.
column4: From west ground-floor delivery access via the central west–east spine, with north/south branches to selected work-bay unloading stops. On upper floors, route from feasible vertical-transfer arrival points; 0.75–1.0 m buffer per side and 1.5 m radius at docking/transfer stops.
column5: IFC: IfcSlab, IfcColumn, IfcGrid; obstacle-free route graph. Access, transfer, and delivery targets explicitly assumed; frame IFC has no stairs. Evidence: IFC + logistics assumptions

column2: Check identifiers, counts and locations of structural materials at distributed floor-level laydown areas.
column4: Six temporary material laydown bays: one near the west end and one near the east end on each of 1F, 2F and 3F. In every bay, retain accessible patrol aisles 0.5–1.5 m outward from storage stacks and entry/turning positions; exclude stacks.
column5: IFC-constrained placement: IfcSlab support and IfcColumn obstacles on each floor; specify six spatially separate laydown polygons; check loading capacity, clearance and access. Evidence: Assumed six zones; IFC-constrained

column2: Identify and sort light structural construction waste at distributed floor-level presorting points.
column3: Mobile C&D waste collection and sorting robot
column4: Six small waste receiving/presorting bays: west and east end on each of 1F–3F, distinct from the six material bays. Prioritize 1.5–2.0 m radius around each feed/sorting station plus short safe access lanes; upper-floor waste subsequently transfers to ground level.
column5: IFC-constrained placement: IfcSlab and IfcColumn; six independent station footprints and haul routes; exclude slab holes, egress paths and material zones. Evidence: Assumed six zones; IFC-constrained

column2: Patrol and visually document temporary edge/opening protection, obstruction hazards and site-safety conditions.
column4: Each floor: west-side access → central west–east safe patrol spine → short north/south branches to selected slab-edge/opening protection viewpoints. Retain route corridor 0.75–1.0 m per side and 1.0 m-radius observation positions; stand back from unprotected edges.
column5: IFC: IfcSlab geometry, IfcOpeningElement voiding IfcSlab, IfcColumn; select safe viewpoints and patrol routes. Temporary guards/cover status is not inferable from absent IFC elements. Evidence: IFC + safety inspection assumptions

column1: Label: Note Priority definition: Priority regions represent planning-level robot working positions and repeatedly traversed corridors, not verified trajectories; buffers/station radii are study-defined, not universal values. Design status: Floor-specific assumption Temporary-facility assumption: 1F–3F east/west six material and six waste zones are per stage, not 12 different scenarios. IFC scope: No IfcSpace or IfcCovering in the inspected enclosure file; building-use labels and finishes are assumptions. Literature evidence: References support task and general workspace principles; exact geometry and 2:1 weights require experimental validation.
